A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the MMTT dataset and ForgeryTalker framework despite the changed title. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–I are available for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original dataset statistics, model comparisons, and FPN ablations in Section 5 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, cross-dataset evaluations, qualitative comparisons, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: V2 adds forgery-aware pretraining with masked language modeling, text generation, segmentation, and contrastive objectives before FPN-guided report generation. V1 trains the FPN and then fine-tunes the Q-former and mask decoder without this additional stage. The underlying FPN, InstructBLIP, and SAM-based components are retained.

E1.justification: MMTT expands from face swapping and inpainting to include semantic attribute editing using StyleCLIP and HFGI, increasing from 128,303 to 152,217 samples. V2 also evaluates transfer to DQ_F++ and the facial-manipulation subset of SynthScars, whereas v1 evaluates only MMTT.

E2.justification: The original SCA, LISA-7B, Osprey, and InstructBLIP comparisons remain. V2 additionally evaluates FFAA, FakeShield, PSCC-NET, IML-ViT, and general vision-language models including Seed1.5VL, Qwen2.5VL, LLaVA, and InternVL3 in Tables 2 and 6.

E3.justification: V2 introduces zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation, separates untuned general vision-language models from MMTT-trained methods, evaluates multiple model sizes, and trains on restricted manipulation-type subsets while testing on the full test set. The existing 8:1:1 split and reported FPN/main-model training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds pretraining ablation, leave-one-manipulation-type-out analysis, cross-dataset generalization tests, and qualitative comparisons with InstructBLIP. The original prompt/oracle ablation remains with updated results. V1's FPN loss/discount-factor analysis is retained unchanged as v2 Table 7, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for its experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces ForgeryTalker's 21.5 CIDEr and 70.81 IoU with 59.3 and 73.67, alongside extensively revised comparator scores. Changed data and training prevent interpreting these as controlled version-to-version gains. V2 adds transfer results, including 113.3 CIDEr on DQ_F++ and 2.20 on SynthScars, plus new ablation outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds mathematical definitions for the pretraining objectives and their weighted combination. Section 3.4 corrects v1's malformed mask-loss expression to summed pixel-wise binary cross-entropy. Existing FPN equations and the PLM definition are retained; neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a facial-forgery dataset and a model jointly producing masks and explanations; renaming this task does not establish a new objective. V2 expands the claimed dataset contribution to attribute editing and adds an explicit contribution claim about complementary effects between localization and report generation.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting pretraining to multimodal representations and manipulation categories to report quality and localization. It attributes low SynthScars scores to annotation-style differences. New limitations discuss training overhead and the absence of binary detection outputs, while the original FPN-quality bottleneck remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 changes reported hardware from four A100s to one H100 and newly specifies Flan-T5-XL, approximately 4B parameters, 48 GPU-hours, and the evaluation toolkit. Some earlier mask-generation and training details disappear. Appendix I introduces vetted academic access under a DUA and withholding generation pipelines, qualifying v1's general public-release promise.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens engagement with explainable forensics, contemporary vision-language models, and multimodal misinformation research. Appendix A newly contrasts MMTT's human annotations with FakeShield's synthetic annotations. References also expand to attribute-editing methods and external evaluation resources; the original three related-work themes remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions, and substantial dataset exposition are rewritten around attribution reports. Related work and experimental setup move into appendices, dataset statistics are reorganized, and dedicated limitations and statements sections are added. This constitutes substantial narrative restructuring beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the dataset overview and statistics, expands the architecture diagram into two training stages, and separates the FPN diagram. It adds qualitative comparisons, dataset examples, and a word cloud. Tables gain explicit zero-shot/fine-tuning groupings and additional transfer and ablation displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow, single-dataset validation through dedicated forgery baselines, two external transfer tests, and analyses of pretraining and data composition. These make generalization and component contributions more assessable. Important weaknesses remain: pretraining settings are incomplete, Table 9's full-set scores differ unexplained from Table 2, and some best-score claims conflict with table entries. These reporting problems qualify the substantial improvement in evaluative depth.
